question: Prescribing a dopamine antagonist (e.g., haloperidol or metoclopramide) to a patient with a parkinsonian syndrome is appropriate first-line management to reduce tremor.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Dopamine antagonists are absolutely contraindicated in parkinsonian syndromes. They block D2 receptors in the striatum, worsening the dopamine deficit and exacerbating all cardinal features. They are used for chorea and tics, not parkinsonism.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct that this is FALSE. Dopamine antagonists will substantially worsen all parkinsonian features (bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor) by further reducing dopaminergic tone in an already depleted system. They are contraindicated in parkinsonian syndromes.
